results.title: Unlimited-OCR by Baidu: Open Source OCR for Long PDFs
excerpts:
It works, but it is page-by-page labor, and the model's memory grows with every token produced until a long document becomes more of an engineering problem than a reading one.

Unlimited-OCR, the open source model released by Baidu on June 18, 2026, sets out to remove that very ritual. The stated goal sits right in the repository subtitle: "Welcome the Era of One-shot Long-horizon Parsing," meaning reading a long document in a single pass instead of splitting and stitching it. The project has gathered 4,663 stars on GitHub as of June 24, 2026, ships under the MIT license, and presents itself as a direct evolution of DeepSeek-OCR. In this article I answer the three practical questions that matter: is it free, how do you use it, and how do you try it right now.

Unlimited-OCR by Baidu - open source MIT OCR model for parsing long PDFs in a single pass Unlimited-OCR: one-shot parsing of long documents, MIT license, open weights on Hugging Face.

**TL;DR for the five-minute reader**
* **Yes, it is free** : MIT license, open weights downloadable from Hugging Face and ModelScope, no API key and no licensing cost.
* **3 billion parameters** in BF16 format and a 32,768-token context window: it runs on a single mid-range NVIDIA GPU.
* **Technical novelty** : it keeps the entire document visible to the model but carries only a sliding window of the generated text, so memory does not grow with every output token.
* **Two ways to use it** : the Transformers library in Python for a single image, or the `infer.py` command-line script for folders and multipage PDFs.
* **Try it instantly** : the Hugging Face Space demo runs in the browser with nothing to install; alternatively Google Colab or Kaggle with a free GPU.

## What Unlimited-OCR Is and Where It Comes From

Unlimited-OCR is a vision-language OCR (Optical Character Recognition, the optical recognition of characters) model: it takes the image of a page as input and returns structured text, including tables and layout.

...

The license is MIT, one of the most permissive around: you can use it, modify it, redistribute it, and even integrate it into a commercial product, provided you keep the copyright notice. There is no official paid API, no key required, and no call limits imposed by the maker.

The model weights live on two platforms: the `baidu/Unlimited-OCR` repository on Hugging Face and the twin version on ModelScope, the equivalent Chinese platform. Both allow a direct download with no paid registration.

The cost, if anything, is the hardware. Running a 3-billion-parameter model requires a GPU, and here there are three concrete scenarios. The first is the local GPU: an NVIDIA card with at least 8-12 GB of VRAM handles the model without trouble, although the minimum figure is not officially stated and depends on document length. The second is the free cloud: Google Colab and Kaggle offer GPUs like the 16 GB T4, more than enough to try the model at zero cost.
The third is renting GPUs by the hour on cloud providers, useful for high volumes. On this topic it is worth reading the case for local inference as a strategic choice , which explains why keeping models on your own machine is coming back into fashion.

## How to Use It: Two Paths

The project offers two ways to use it, designed for different needs. The first is the Hugging Face Transformers library, ideal for embedding the model inside a Python script or a service. The second is the `infer.py` command-line script, built to process whole folders of images or PDFs in batch.

You start by installing the dependencies. The repository pins precise versions to guarantee reproducibility, so it is best to respect them inside a dedicated virtual environment.

install.sh BASH copy

```
# clone the repository and create the environment 
 git clone https://github.com/baidu/Unlimited-OCR
 cd Unlimited-OCR
 python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate

 # dependencies with pinned versions
pip install torch== 2.10.0 torchvision== 0.25.0 transformers== 4.57.1 Pillow== 12.1.1 pymupdf einops
```

At this point the model is ready. For a single image just a few lines of Python are enough: you load the tokenizer and the model from Hugging Face, move it to the GPU, and call the `infer` method with the image path.

ocr\_single.py PYTHON copy

```
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer
 import torch

model_name = 'baidu/Unlimited-OCR' 
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer. from_pretrained (model_name, trust_remote_code= True )
model = AutoModel. from_pretrained (
    model_name, trust_remote_code= True ,
    torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16
). eval (). cuda ()

 # gundam mode: fast, suited to dense pages 
model. infer (tokenizer, prompt= '<image>document parsing.' ,
    image_file= 'document.jpg' , base_size= 1024 ,
    image_size= 640 , crop_mode= True , max_length= 32768 )
```

The `prompt` parameter steers the task: `document parsing.` requests full extraction with layout.

...

PDF files are handled thanks to PyMuPDF, the library the project uses to convert pages into images before recognition. The `--concurrency` parameter controls how many pages are processed in parallel: raising it speeds up the work but consumes more VRAM, so it has to be tuned to the available GPU. The output lands in the indicated folder, one entry per document, already clean and ready to index in your RAG's vector database.

On the inference-engine front, beyond Transformers the repository also documents support for SGLang with a custom logit processor that avoids n-gram repetitions, a useful detail when serving high volumes and aiming to maximize throughput.

## How to Test It Right Now Without Installing Anything

Not everyone has a GPU at hand, and the good news is you do not need one to get a feel for it. There are three paths, from the fastest to the most complete.

### Three ways to try it today

* **Hugging Face Space (zero setup):** the official demo runs in the browser.
You upload an image or a PDF and get the text back, with nothing to install. It is by far the fastest way. Just check that the Space is awake: free Spaces often go to sleep and take a few seconds to wake up.
* **Google Colab or Kaggle (free GPU):** open a notebook, paste the Python snippet above, and use the free T4 GPU on offer. Ideal for testing on your own documents without spending a cent.
* **Local install (full control):** with an NVIDIA GPU, follow the install commands and process documents on your own machine, data that never leaves your computer.

The in-browser demo is the recommended starting point: in a minute you can tell whether the recognition quality fits your documents, before writing a single line of code. If your files are confidential, though, skip straight to the local install or a private notebook, so the scans are never uploaded to a third-party service.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

#### 1\. Is Unlimited-OCR really free even for commercial use?

**Yes.

...

**Both.** The `infer.py` script uses PyMuPDF to convert PDF pages into images before recognition, so it accepts both image files (JPG, PNG) and multipage PDF documents in a single run.

#### 5\. What is the difference between gundam and base mode?

**It is a trade-off between speed and accuracy.** The gundam mode works at 640 resolution with cropping, is faster, and is fine for text-dense pages. The base mode works at 1024 on the whole page, is more accurate on intricate layouts and multipage documents, but heavier.

#### 6\. How large is the model to download?

**About 6 GB.** With 3 billion parameters in BF16 format the weights take up roughly 6 GB on disk. The exact size depends on the files published on Hugging Face, but it stays in an order of magnitude that a normal connection and disk can handle.

## Conclusions

Unlimited-OCR is not the first OCR based on vision-language models, but it tackles the right problem in the right way.

## Conclusion: A New Era of Document AI

Baidu's Unlimited OCR is more than just a better OCR tool. It's a rethinking of how AI models should handle long-horizon tasks — by mimicking the way human working memory actually functions, rather than brute-forcing through unlimited context windows.

For businesses dealing with large document archives, legal firms processing contracts, researchers digitizing books, or anyone who's ever been frustrated by page-limit restrictions in OCR tools — this is a genuine game-changer.

The era of one-shot, full-document parsing has arrived.

# Run Baidu Unlimited-OCR Locally: Transformers, vLLM & SGLang (2026 Guide)

Baidu's Unlimited-OCR parses entire multi-page PDFs in a single forward pass. Here's how to run the 3.3B open-weights model locally with Transformers, vLLM, or SGLang.

Published 05 Jul 2026 • Updated 05 Jul 2026 • 4 min read

**Quick answer.** Unlimited-OCR is Baidu's MIT-licensed 3.3B vision-language OCR model, released June 22, 2026. Its headline trick is one-shot multi-page parsing: it transcribes an entire PDF in a single forward pass instead of page-by-page. Run it locally via Hugging Face Transformers, the official vLLM Docker image ( `vllm/vllm-openai:unlimited-ocr` ), or SGLang — a single 12 GB+ consumer GPU is enough.

DeepSeek-OCR started the "optical compression" wave in 2025. Baidu's [Unlimited-OCR](https://github.com/baidu/Unlimited-OCR?ref=codersera.
com) — the team explicitly says it aims to push DeepSeek-OCR one step further — is the strongest follow-up so far: over one million Hugging Face downloads in its first two weeks, a top-3 trending slot, and one of the most upvoted r/LocalLLaMA threads of late June 2026.

This guide covers what the model actually does differently, the hardware you need, and three working local setups: plain Transformers, vLLM, and SGLang.

## What is Unlimited-OCR?

Unlimited-OCR is a 3.3B-parameter image-text-to-text model from Baidu, released under the MIT license on June 22, 2026, with the paper ( [arXiv 2606.23050](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23050?ref=codersera.com) , "Unlimited OCR Works") following a day later. It converts document images — scans, screenshots, photographed pages, handwriting — into clean structured text and Markdown/LaTeX.

The release timeline moved unusually fast, which tells you how much backing it has:

* **June 22:** weights on Hugging Face (MIT license)
* **June 23:** paper on arXiv + ModelScope mirror
* **June 24:** free [Hugging Face Spaces demo](https://huggingface.co/spaces/baidu/Unlimited-OCR?ref=codersera.com)
* **June 28:** official vLLM support with prebuilt Docker images
* **July 3:** hosted API on Baidu Cloud

## Why is one-shot multi-page parsing a big deal?

Every practical OCR pipeline until now — DeepSeek-OCR included — processes documents page-by-page: split the PDF, run the model N times, stitch the outputs back together. That loses cross-page context (tables that continue across a page break, footnotes, running headers) and multiplies overhead.

Unlimited-OCR's "long-horizon parsing" mode accepts dozens of page images in a _single_ forward pass and emits one coherent transcript. Community tests have shown it turning a handwritten calculus exam into clean LaTeX and parsing complex multi-page PDFs in one go — including non-Latin scripts (it's genuinely multilingual, with users confirming solid Cyrillic support).

...

It's trained multilingually — community tests confirm strong results on Cyrillic documents and even handwritten math converted to LaTeX. As with any OCR model, extremely low-quality scans still degrade output.

### Is there a hosted option if I don't want to self-host?

Yes — a free Hugging Face Spaces demo for quick tests, and a hosted API on Baidu Cloud since July 3, 2026. For privacy-sensitive documents, local inference via vLLM remains the better choice.

Self-hosting more than just OCR? Our [self-hosting LLMs complete guide](https://codersera.com/blog/self-hosting-llms-complete-guide-2026/) covers the full stack — hardware sizing, serving engines, and quantization — for running open models in production.
